While she initially claimed that the children were taken during a carjacking incident and publicly pleaded for their safe return, the case sustained a drastic twist when it was revealed that she made the whole story up and was actually responsible for the murder of her own children.

Following her second parole hearing in November 2026, Us breaks down everything to know about the case, her deplorable claims and where she is today, below.

Where Is Susan Smith Today? 
 Susan admitted she killed her children on November 3, 1994, just nine days after she fatally drowned her sons, Michael Daniel Smith, 3, and Alexander Tyler Smith, 14 months. Michael and Alexander’s bodies were later recovered on November 4, 1994.

items.title: KJ Biermann's Alleged Victim to Testify at Trial in Sexual Battery Case
items.summary:
KJ Biermann ’s alleged victim will testify at trial amid his sexual battery case.

According to court documents obtained by Us , the alleged victim “will be made available to testify at trial and be subject to cross-examination.” Other witnesses who will offer testimony include the alleged victim’s parents and grandmother, the doctor who treated the alleged victim after the alleged assault and the officers who responded to the complaint.

The State of Georgia filed a motion to block Biermann’s defense from introducing character evidence as part of a “reverse propensity defense.” The documents viewed by Us reveal that the State “anticipates the defendant may attempt to offer evidence at trial through his own testimony or the testimony of witnesses offered by the defendant, as to the defendant’s interactions with other children or underage girls, other than the victim in the instant case, and the defendant’s reputation for good behavior around children.”

Prosecutors also filed a motion invoking the Rape Shield Stature, which aims to prohibit the defense from entering evidence detailing the alleged victim’s prior sexual behavior.

According to the document, “evidence relating to the past sexual behavior of the complaining witness shall not be admissible, either as direct evidence or on cross-examination of the complaining witness or other witnesses.”

items.title: Mom Says She 'Should Have Stayed Home' After Drunk Driving Crash Kills Son
items.summary:
A Minnesota mother will spend the next several years in prison after she killed her youngest child when she drunkenly crashed her SUV into a ditch.

A Ramsey County district judge sentenced Rachale Peloquin to serve four years in prison on Monday, November 16, after she was convicted of criminal vehicular homicide for negligently driving while under the influence of alcohol for her involvement in September, according to the Pioneer Press .

Prior to the sentencing, Peloquin, 28, and her attorney asked that she receive probation instead of prison time.

“Despite my best effort to save him, I could not,” Peloquin reportedly said about her “sweet baby” Raevon Melvin Anthony Todd during the sentencing. Raevon was just 1 year old when he died in the crash.

Mom Allegedly Poisons Her 2-Month-Old Baby to Death With Alcohol 

“[Raevon] depended on his mother to protect him,” Assistant Ramsey County Attorney Daphneyse Marcelin told the court, per the outlet. “Remorse does not undo his death.”

“My sweet baby Raevon is no longer here,” Peloquin said during her sentencing hearing. “I should have stayed home with my kids, and my baby Raevon would be OK. I’m sorry to everyone who lost him that day.”

The incident took place in September 2025 when Peloquin was driving with her three children and another adult passenger in Maplewood, Minnesota. She crashed her vehicle around 6:30 p.m. after she turned onto Highway 61, according to an incident report viewed by Us .

items.title: Kim Zolciak Facing 6-Figure Default Judgment Over Defunct Business
items.summary:
Kim Zolciak could be on the hook for six figures over her now-defunct business amid her son Kroy “KJ” Biermann Jr .’s sexual battery case.

Court documents obtained exclusively by Us show that Headway Capital requested a default judgment against Zolciak, 48, on Tuesday, November 17 — and it could cost her a pretty penny.

The financial institution sued the Real Housewives of Atlanta alum in April, claiming she entered into a business-use line of credit and security agreement for 8 Busy B’s LLC and allegedly failed to repay $75,000.

Now, Headway Capital is asking for that amount plus thousands more after Zolciak “failed to file any responsive pleadings” to the lawsuit, according to the docs obtained by Us .

items.title: Susan Smith Denied Parole 30 Years After Drowning Sons in South Carolina Lake
items.summary:
Susan Smith was unanimously denied parole 30 years after she admitted to killing her sons days following her fabricated claim the boys were taken in a carjacking incident.

Smith, 55, virtually appeared in court on Thursday, November 19, where she asked to be granted parole . A forensic psychiatrist, a prison guard and two of her brothers spoke on her behalf, while her ex-husband, David Smith , argued that she should not be granted parole during the hearing.

David said that Susan being released would be “a huge injustice” to their sons, Michael and Alex, according to WBTV .

In 1994, Sysan rolled her car with Michael and Alex strapped into the vehicle into John D. Long Lake in South Carolina. The boys – who were just 3 years old and 14 months old at the time – died, and Susan initially claimed the boys had been taken in a carjacking incident.

Mom Found Guilty of Killing 2 Sons, Setting Their Minnesota Home Ablaze 

Susan made national headlines when she publicly pleaded for the safe return of her sons, but admitted nine days later that she had killed them.

One year later, Susan was sentenced to serve life in prison with the possibility of parole after 30 years.

The latest hearing marks the second time Susan was eligible for parole. She was first eligible in November 2024, but it was determined that she would stay in custody after the board unanimously denied her request. At the time, only six of the 471 letters and emails received by the parole board supported her release.

items.title: Mom Left Babysitter's Body in Cemetery After She Went to Watch Kids, Was Shot
items.summary:
A Virginia mother abandoned a 17-year-old’s body in a cemetery after the girl arrived at the woman’s home to babysit her children and was shot, prosecutors said.

Now, more than seven years later, Simone Worrell has been sentenced to 26 years in prison on murder and other charges in Nye’Tazia Hicks’ death, per The Virginian-Pilot .

Hicks was shot in the torso after she arrived at Worrell’s Portsmouth home to watch Worrell’s children, while other juveniles were also at the residence the evening of July 27, 2019, according to the Portsmouth Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office .

One of the children ultimately accessed an unsecured gun from a hallway closet.

Babysitter Sentenced for Murdering Missing Boy After She Helped With Search 

Hicks tried to take the gun away from the juvenile, but the weapon went off, striking Hicks and causing both of them to fall backward, prosecutors said.

The boy tried to put pressure on Hicks’ wound and went to call 911, but Worrell intervened and told him not to call for help, according to prosecutors. Afterward, he fled the home.

The boy was Domonique White, who was 14 and ran to his parents’ home not far from Worrell’s residence, The Virginian-Pilot reported.

White, now 21, testified against Worrell at trial in February and reportedly said he had retrieved the gun from Worrell’s closet to show the firearm to Hicks, whom he said he had been dating.

“Being a kid back in the day, I thought it was cool,” White said, per the newspaper. “We were messing around.”

After stopping White from getting help, Worrell took Hicks’ body to Evergreen…
items.t: Mom Left Babysitter's Body in Cemetery After She Went to Watch Kids, Was Shot

items.title: 2 Texas Men Dead After Hostage Situation Ends in Apparent Murder-Suicide
items.summary:
Two men were found dead inside of a home in Gillespie County, Texas, after a hostage situation resulted in an apparent murder-suicide, according to authorities.

The Gillespie County Sheriff’s Office said in a press release shared via Facebook that deputies responded to a home on Cemetery Road in Stonewall, Texas, shortly after 5 p.m. on Wednesday, November 18, after they received reports of a disturbance that involved a man with a gun.

Deputies began communicating with the victim inside the residence via phone during the incident, and he told deputies that an armed man would not allow him to leave the home.

Because the incident was treated as a hostage situation, deputies made multiple attempts to communicate with both the suspect and victim so that the conflict could hopefully end in a peaceful resolution.

Argument Between Roommates Leads to Murder-Suicide in Las Vegas, Says Police 

Authorities said they lost communication with the men for several hours. Law enforcement then entered the home around 3:30 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, and they found both men dead in a room.

Investigators ultimately determined that the incident was a murder-suicide involving a 35-year-old suspect and a 49-year-old victim.

The Gillespie County Sheriff’s Office said that they worked on the case with the help of the Kerr County Sheriff’s Office Special Operations Unit, Texas Department of Public Safety Special Operations Unit and a Texas Ranger.

Authorities have not yet released the men’s identities as they await to notify next of kin. It’s not currently clear how the two men knew each…
items.t: 2 Texas Men Dead After Hostage Situation Ends in Apparent Murder-Suicide
